source_text: Nam et prophetare et daemonia excludere et virtutes magnas in terris facere sublimis utique et admirabilis res est, non tamen regnum coeleste consequitur quisquis in his omnibus invenitur, nisi recti et justi itineris observatione gradiatur. Denuntiat Dominus et dicit: Multi mihi dicent in illo die: Domine, Domine, nonne in tuo nomine prophetavimus, et in tuo nomine daemonia exclusimus, et in nomine tuo virtutes magnas fecimus? Et tunc dicam illis: Numquam vos cognovi; recedite a me, qui operamini iniquitatem. Justitia opus est ut promereri quis possit Deum judicem: praeceptis ejus et monitis obtemperandum est, ut accipiant merita nostra mercedem. Dominus in Evangelio suo, cum spei et fidei nostrae viam compendio breviante dirigeret: Dominus Deus tuus, inquit, Deus unus est; et: Diliges Dominum Deum tuum de toto corde tuo, et de tota anima tua, et de tota virtute tua. Hoc est primum mandatum; et secundum simile huic: Diliges proximum tuum tamquam te. In his duobus praeceptis tota lex pendet et prophetae. Unitatem simul et dilectionem magisterio suo docuit, prophetas omnes et legem praeceptis duobus inclusit. Quam vero unitatem servat, quam dilectionem custodit aut cogitat, qui, discordiae furore vesanus, Ecclesiam scindit, fidem destruit, pacem turbat, charitatem dissipat, sacramentum profanat?
pass_a_gloss: For both to prophesy and to cast out demons and to perform great deeds on earth is indeed a sublime and admirable thing, but nevertheless the kingdom of heaven is not attained by whoever is found in all these things, unless they walk in the observation of a right and just path. The Lord announces and says: Many will say to me on that day: Lord, Lord, did we not prophesy in your name, and cast out demons in your name, and perform great deeds in your name? And then I will say to them: I never knew you; depart from me, you who work iniquity. Righteousness is necessary so that someone may merit God the judge: His precepts and admonitions must be obeyed, so that our merits may receive a reward. The Lord, in His Gospel, while directing the way of our hope and faith in a brief summary, says: The Lord your God is one God; and: You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your strength. This is the first commandment; and the second is similar to it: You shall love your neighbor as yourself. On these two commandments the entire law and the prophets depend. He taught unity and love simultaneously through His teaching, and included all the prophets and the law in two commandments. But who is it that preserves unity, who guards or considers love, when, maddened by the fury of discord, they split the Church, destroy faith, disturb peace, dissipate charity, and profane the sacrament?

pass_b_english: To prophesy, cast out demons, and perform great works on earth is certainly a sublime and admirable thing, yet no one attains the kingdom of heaven merely by being found in all these things unless they walk in the observance of a right and just path (Matt 7:21-23). The Lord warns and says: "Many will say to me on that day, 'Lord, Lord, did we not prophesy in your name, cast out demons in your name, and perform great works in your name?' Then I will tell them plainly, 'I never knew you; depart from me, you who practice lawlessness.'" Righteousness is necessary so that anyone may merit God as judge; we must obey His precepts and admonitions so that our merits may receive their reward. In His Gospel, the Lord directed the way of our hope and faith with a brief summary: "The Lord your God is one" (Deut 6:4), and "You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your strength" (Deut 6:5). "This is the first commandment; and the second is like it: You shall love your neighbor as yourself" (Mark 12:29-31). On these two commandments hang the whole Law and the Prophets. He taught unity and love together through His teaching, embracing all the prophets and the Law within two commandments. But who preserves that unity, who guards or even considers that love, when, driven mad by the fury of discord, they tear apart the Church, destroy faith, disturb peace, dissipate charity, and profane the sacrament?
